title: Epic: Pi-Tainá MVP — Telegram biodiversity bot on Pi agent
description:
## Goal
Build a self-hosted Telegram bot (Pi-Tainá) that replicates core Tainá functionality as a Pi agent. Each community deploys their own instance on a Mac Mini with their own Telegram bot token and ATProto community account.

## Architecture
- **Telegram**: grammY library for Telegram Bot API
- **Agent**: Pi coding agent SDK (`@mariozechner/pi-coding-agent`) with `createAgentSession()`
- **ATProto**: Single community account using `@atproto/api` with app password auth (not OAuth)
- **Models**: API-based (Anthropic/OpenAI/Google keys via Pi's provider system)
- **Deployment**: Self-hosted on Mac Mini M4, easy setup

## Core Features (MVP)
1. Species identification from photos (vision AI)
2. Photo quality coaching (organism-specific tips)
3. Publish Darwin Core occurrence records to community ATProto PDS
4. Geocoding via Nominatim (+ Telegram location sharing)
5. General community assistant (collective intelligence)
6. Self-extending: communities can ask Tainá to build new skills

## Key Design Decisions
- One ATProto account per community (not per user)
- Telegram user info (ID, username, display name) stored in Darwin Core `recordedBy` field
- Per-user sessions within the community
- Groups: responds only when @mentioned or when photos are sent
- DMs: always responds
- Community personality customizable via AGENTS.md / skills
- All Tainás share core primitives, each community customizes personality/language/local knowledge

## Success Criteria
- Bot responds to DMs and group @mentions
- Photos auto-trigger species identification + coaching
- Users can publish observations to ATProto PDS via inline keyboards
- Telegram location sharing works for coordinates
- Easy setup: clone repo, set env vars, run one command

- outDir: ./dist, rootDir: ./src

**.gitignore:**
Standard Node.js gitignore + .env, .env.local, dist/, node_modules/, data/

**src/index.ts:**
Just `console.log("pi-taina starting...");` as placeholder.

title: README.md — Setup and deployment guide
description:
## Files
- README.md (create)

## What to do
Create a comprehensive README for Pi-Tainá that explains what it is, how to set it up, and how to deploy it on a Mac Mini.

**Sections:**

1. **Header**: Pi-Tainá logo area (just text for now), one-line description: "A self-hosted Telegram bot for community biodiversity documentation, powered by Pi agent"

2. **What is Pi-Tainá?**: 
   - Community biodiversity AI assistant on Telegram
   - Identifies species from photos, coaches on photo quality, publishes Darwin Core occurrence records
   - Each community runs their own instance with their own personality
   - Built on Pi coding agent — communities can ask Tainá to build new capabilities
   - Part of the GainForest network

3. **Quick Start** (numbered steps):
   - Prerequisites: Node.js 20+, npm
   - Clone the repo
   - `npm install`
   - Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and fill in values
   - `npm start`

4. **Configuration** (env vars table):
   | Variable | Required | Description |
   | TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN | Yes | From @BotFather on Telegram |
   | ANTHROPIC_API_KEY | Yes | Anthropic API key for Claude |
   | ATPROTO_HANDLE | No* | Community ATProto/Bluesky handle |
   | ATPROTO_PASSWORD | No* | App password for the ATProto account |
   | PI_MODEL | No | Override default model (default: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514) |
   | SPECIES_ID_MODEL | No | Model for species identification (default: claude-sonnet-4-20250514) |
   
   *Required for publishing observations

5. **Setting up Telegram Bot**: 
   - Message @BotFather on Telegram
   - /newbot, choose name and username
   - Copy the token
   - Optional: set bot description and profile photo

6. **Setting up ATProto Account**:
   - Create a Bluesky account for your community (e.g., taina-amazon.bsky.social)
   - Go to Settings → App Passwords → Create app password
   - Use the handle and app password in .env

7. **Customizing for Your Community**:
   - Edit AGENTS.md to customize personality, language, local knowledge
   - Add skills in ./skills/ directory
   - Tainá can also build skills herself when asked

8. **How It Works** (brief architecture):
   - Telegram message → Pi agent → AI response
   - Photos auto-trigger species identification
   - Observations published to ATProto PDS as Darwin Core records

9. **Running as a Service** (Mac Mini deployment):
   - Using pm2: `npm install -g pm2 && pm2 start npm --name taina -- start`
   - Auto-restart on crash, startup on boot: `pm2 startup && pm2 save`

10. **License**: MIT (or whatever GainForest uses)

## Dont
- Do NOT include development/contributing instructions yet
- Do NOT include Docker setup (future work)
- Do NOT include complex deployment options beyond pm2
- Do NOT reference taina-v3-2 or the web app
acceptance_criteria: README.md exists. Contains: project description, quick start steps, env var configuration table, Telegram bot setup instructions, ATProto account setup instructions, community customization guide, pm2 deployment instructions. All env vars from .env.example are documented.
notes: IMPORTANT: The required AI key is GEMINI_API_KEY (Google Gemini), NOT ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Update the config table accordingly. Anthropic and OpenAI are optional alternative providers.
close_reason: 9c1388c add README with setup and deployment guide

title: Validate env vars and create .env.example with all project variables
description:
## Files
- .env.example (create)
- src/env.ts (create)

## What to do
Create the definitive environment variable configuration for the entire Pi-Tainá project. This task must be done FIRST before any other work.

### 1. Create `.env.example` with ALL project variables:

```env
# ============================================
# Pi-Tainá Environment Configuration
# ============================================
# Copy this file to .env and fill in your values:
#   cp .env.example .env
# ============================================

# --- REQUIRED ---

# Telegram Bot Token (get from @BotFather on Telegram)
TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=

# Google Gemini API Key (used for both the conversational agent and species identification)
# Get from: https://aistudio.google.com/apikey
GEMINI_API_KEY=

# --- ATPROTO (required for publishing observations) ---

# Community ATProto/Bluesky handle
# Example: taina-amazon.bsky.social
ATPROTO_HANDLE=

# App password for the ATProto account (NOT your main password)
# Generate at: Bluesky → Settings → App Passwords → Add App Password
ATPROTO_PASSWORD=

# ATProto service URL (default: https://bsky.social)
# Change this if your community runs its own PDS
# ATPROTO_SERVICE=https://bsky.social

# --- OPTIONAL: Alternative AI Providers ---
# Set these to use models from other providers via Pi agent

# Anthropic API Key (enables Claude models)
# ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=

# OpenAI API Key (enables GPT models)
# OPENAI_API_KEY=

# --- OPTIONAL: Model Overrides ---

# Override the default conversational model (Pi agent)
# Format: provider/model-id
# PI_MODEL=google/gemini-2.5-flash

# Override the model used for species identification
# Must be a Gemini model ID (e.g., gemini-2.5-flash, gemini-2.5-pro)
# SPECIES_ID_MODEL=gemini-2.5-flash

# --- OPTIONAL: Pi Agent Configuration ---

# Override Pi config directory (default: ~/.pi/agent)
# PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR=

# Extended prompt cache retention (set to "long" for extended caching)
# PI_CACHE_RETENTION=long

# Skip Pi version check at startup (set to "1" to skip)
# PI_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK=1
```

### 2. Create `src/env.ts` — centralized env var validation and access:

```typescript
// Centralized environment variable access for Pi-Tainá
// All env var reads go through this module — no process.env scattered in code

export interface EnvConfig {
  // Required
  telegramBotToken: string;
  geminiApiKey: string;
  
  // ATProto (optional — publishing disabled without these)
  atprotoHandle: string | undefined;
  atprotoPassword: string | undefined;
  atprotoService: string; // defaults to "https://bsky.social"
  
  // Optional AI providers (for Pi agent multi-model support)
  anthropicApiKey: string | undefined;
  openaiApiKey: string | undefined;
  
  // Model overrides
  piModel: string;           // defaults to "google/gemini-2.5-flash"
  speciesIdModel: string;    // defaults to "gemini-2.5-flash"
}

// Validate required env vars and return typed config
// Throws with descriptive error listing ALL missing vars (not just the first one)
export function loadEnvConfig(): EnvConfig

// Check if ATProto publishing is configured
export function isAtprotoConfigured(config: EnvConfig): boolean
// Returns true only if BOTH atprotoHandle AND atprotoPassword are set
```

**`loadEnvConfig()` behavior:**
- Reads all env vars from `process.env`
- Required vars: `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`
- Collects ALL missing required vars, then throws a single error listing them all:
  `"Missing required environment variables: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, GEMINI_API_KEY"`
- For optional vars: returns undefined if not set
- For vars with defaults: applies the default
- `atprotoService`: reads `ATPROTO_SERVICE`, defaults to `"https://bsky.social"`
- `piModel`: reads `PI_MODEL`, defaults to `"google/gemini-2.5-flash"`
- `speciesIdModel`: reads `SPECIES_ID_MODEL`, defaults to `"gemini-2.5-flash"`
- `geminiApiKey`: reads `GEMINI_API_KEY`

**Important:** This module does NOT call `dotenv`. The caller (index.ts) does `import "dotenv/config"` before calling `loadEnvConfig()`.

## Dont
- Do NOT call dotenv in this module
- Do NOT import any other project modules
- Do NOT add logging — just validation and typed access
- Do NOT add runtime checks beyond what is listed (no API key format validation etc)
- Do NOT use zod or any validation library — plain TypeScript is fine
acceptance_criteria: 1. .env.example exists with ALL variables documented (TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, GEMINI_API_KEY, ATPROTO_HANDLE, ATPROTO_PASSWORD, ATPROTO_SERVICE, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, PI_MODEL, SPECIES_ID_MODEL, PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR, PI_CACHE_RETENTION, PI_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK). 2. GEMINI_API_KEY is the ONLY required AI key (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and OPENAI_API_KEY are optional). 3. src/env.ts exports loadEnvConfig() and isAtprotoConfigured(). 4. loadEnvConfig() throws listing ALL missing required vars if any are missing. 5. loadEnvConfig() returns typed EnvConfig with correct defaults (piModel defaults to "google/gemini-2.5-flash", speciesIdModel defaults to "gemini-2.5-flash"). 6. TypeScript compiles without errors.
close_reason: 04b0db3 feat: add env var validation and .env.example

title: Multi-photo accumulation and coaching loop
description:
## Files
- src/agent.ts (modify)
- src/tools/publish-occurrence.ts (modify)
- AGENTS.md (modify)

## What to do

### 1. src/agent.ts — accumulate photos instead of replacing

Change `SessionState.latestPhoto` to an array:

```typescript
interface SessionState {
  session: AgentSession;
  photos: Array<{ data: Buffer; mimeType: string }>;  // was: latestPhoto?: { data, mimeType }
  currentUser?: TelegramUser;
}
```

**Changes:**
- Initialize `photos: []` when creating a new session state
- In `sendToAgent()`: when msg has a photo, PUSH to `sessionState.photos` (do NOT replace)
- In the `identify_species` tool execute: use the LAST photo in the array (`stateRef.state.photos[stateRef.state.photos.length - 1]`) for identification. If no photos, return error as before.
- In the `publish_occurrence` tool execute: pass ALL photos from `stateRef.state.photos` to publishOccurrence (see below)
- After a successful publish, CLEAR the photos array: `stateRef.state.photos = []`
- Add a new tool `clear_photos` with description "Clear all accumulated photos for the current observation. Use when the user wants to start over or discard photos." — it just sets `stateRef.state.photos = []` and returns a confirmation message.

**Prompt construction in sendToAgent():**
- When msg has a photo: `"The user sent a photo (photo ${sessionState.photos.length} in this observation session). [Photo is available for analysis].${userText}"`

### 2. src/tools/publish-occurrence.ts — support multiple images

Change the interface:

```typescript
export interface OccurrenceInput {
  // ... existing fields ...
  
  // Image (raw bytes, will be uploaded to PDS as blobs)
  // Changed from single to array
  images?: Array<{ data: Buffer; mimeType: string }>;
  
  // REMOVE these:
  // imageData?: Buffer;
  // imageMimeType?: string;
}
```

**Changes to publishOccurrence():**
- Replace the single image upload block with a loop over `input.images`
- Upload each image via `agent.uploadBlob()`, collect all blob refs
- Set `record.imageEvidence = blobRefs.map(ref => ({ file: ref }))`
- Set `record.dcType = "StillImage"` if any images present
- Max 5 images (slice to 5 if more provided, matching the lexicon `.max(5)`)
- If any single upload fails, log the error but continue with the others (dont fail the whole publish)
- Update PublishResult: add `imageCount: number` field

### 3. AGENTS.md — reinforce multi-photo coaching loop

Add a new section after "Photo Quality Coaching Tips" called "Multi-Photo Observation Flow":

```markdown
## Multi-Photo Observation Flow
When coaching on photo quality, actively encourage multiple angles:
- After first photo: identify the species, then suggest 1-2 specific additional angles based on the organism group
- After each additional photo: acknowledge it, note what it adds, suggest more if key features are still missing
- When you have enough good photos (or the user says they are done): offer to publish
- When publishing: ALL accumulated photos are attached to the observation record
- After publishing: photos are cleared for the next observation

Example flow:
- User sends photo of a mushroom from above
- Tainá: "This looks like Amanita muscaria! 🍄 Great top-down shot. Could you also photograph the underside showing the gills? That is the most important feature for confirming mushroom IDs."
- User sends photo of gills
- Tainá: "Perfect, I can see the white free gills clearly! One more — the stem base would help rule out look-alikes. Or we can publish with these 2 photos if you prefer."
- User: "publish it"
- Tainá publishes with both photos attached

Key principles:
- Never demand more photos — always offer to publish with what you have
- Be specific about WHAT to photograph and WHY (not just "take more photos")
- Celebrate each additional photo the user sends
- 2-3 good photos from different angles is ideal, but 1 is fine too
```

## Dont
- Do NOT change the identify_species tool — it still analyzes one photo at a time (the latest one)
- Do NOT change the geocode_location tool
- Do NOT change telegram.ts or env.ts
- Do NOT change the Telegram message handling — photos still come one at a time from Telegram, we just accumulate them
acceptance_criteria: 1. agent.ts SessionState has photos array instead of latestPhoto. 2. Photos accumulate across messages (push, not replace). 3. publish_occurrence tool passes all photos. 4. Photos cleared after successful publish. 5. publish-occurrence.ts accepts images array, uploads multiple blobs, sets imageEvidence as array. 6. Max 5 images enforced. 7. AGENTS.md has multi-photo coaching flow section. 8. clear_photos tool exists. 9. TypeScript compiles. 10. PublishResult has imageCount field.
close_reason: e3371e8 multi-photo accumulation and coaching loop

title: ATProto community account client

## What to do
Create a module that manages the ATProto community account connection using `@atproto/api`.

**Exports:**

```typescript
// Initialize and login to the community ATProto account
// Reads ATPROTO_HANDLE and ATPROTO_PASSWORD from env
// Throws if env vars missing or login fails

// Get the community DID (after login)
```

- Logs success: `"ATProto: logged in as @{handle} ({did})"`
- Throws descriptive error if env vars missing: `"Missing ATPROTO_HANDLE or ATPROTO_PASSWORD in environment"`
- Throws descriptive error if login fails with the upstream error message

## Dont
- Do NOT use OAuth — use simple identifier/password login (app passwords)
- Do NOT import anything from taina-v3-2
- Do NOT add any publishing logic here — that goes in a separate tool

title: Pi agent session manager — per-user sessions with custom tools
description:
## Files
- src/agent.ts (create)

## What to do
Create the Pi agent integration layer. This manages per-user agent sessions and registers Tainá's custom tools with the Pi SDK.

**Export:**

```typescript
import type { IncomingMessage } from "./telegram.ts";

// Get or create a Pi agent session for a Telegram user
// Sessions are keyed by Telegram user ID
// Each session persists to disk under ./data/sessions/{userId}/
export async function getOrCreateSession(userId: number): Promise<AgentSession>

// Send a message to the agent and collect the full response
// Handles: text messages, photo context, location context
// Returns the agent's text response
export async function sendToAgent(
  msg: IncomingMessage
): Promise<string>

// Cleanup / dispose all sessions
export async function disposeAllSessions(): Promise<void>
```

**Behavior:**

1. **Session management**:
   - Maintain a `Map<number, AgentSession>` keyed by Telegram user ID
   - On first message from a user, create a new session via `createAgentSession()`
   - Use `SessionManager.create("./data/sessions/{userId}")` for persistent sessions
   - Configure `AuthStorage.create()` and `ModelRegistry` once at module level

2. **Agent configuration**:
   - Default model: read from env `PI_MODEL` with fallback to `"anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514"`
   - Set API key via `authStorage.setRuntimeApiKey("anthropic", process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)`
   - Also set OpenAI and Google keys if present in env
   - Load AGENTS.md from project root (Pi does this automatically via DefaultResourceLoader)
   - Load skills from `./skills/` directory (Pi does this automatically)

3. **Custom tools registration**:
   Register 3 custom tools via the `customTools` option in `createAgentSession()`:

   **a) `identify_species`**:
   - Description: "Identify a species from a photo that the user sent. Call this when the user sends a photo of a plant, animal, fungus, or other organism."
   - Input schema: `{ userContext?: string }` (the photo data comes from session state, not tool input)
   - Implementation: reads the latest photo from a per-session state store, calls `identifySpecies()` from tools/identify-species.ts, returns the JSON result as a string
   
   **b) `publish_occurrence`**:
   - Description: "Publish a biodiversity occurrence record to the community ATProto PDS. Use after identifying a species when the user confirms they want to publish."
   - Input schema: `{ scientificName: string, vernacularName?: string, decimalLatitude?: number, decimalLongitude?: number, locality?: string, country?: string, countryCode?: string, habitat?: string, behavior?: string, individualCount?: number, occurrenceRemarks?: string, eventDate?: string }`
   - Implementation: calls `publishOccurrence()` from tools/publish-occurrence.ts, passing the tool input + current photo data + current Telegram user from session state
   
   **c) `geocode_location`**:
   - Description: "Convert a text location description to GPS coordinates. Use when the user provides a place name instead of GPS coordinates."
   - Input schema: `{ query: string, countryCode?: string }`
   - Implementation: calls `geocodeLocation()` from tools/geocode-location.ts, returns the result as JSON string

4. **Message construction for sendToAgent()**:
   - If msg has photo: store photo data in per-session state, then prompt with: "The user sent a photo. [Photo is available for analysis]. {msg.text || ""}"
   - If msg has location: prompt with: "The user shared their GPS location: latitude {lat}, longitude {lon}. {msg.text || ""}"
   - If msg has only text: prompt with the text directly
   - The prompt should include user context: "Message from {user.displayName} (Telegram user ID: {user.id})"

5. **Response collection**:
   - Subscribe to session events
   - Collect all `text_delta` events from `message_update` into a string
   - Wait for `agent_end` event
   - Return the collected text

## Dont
- Do NOT handle Telegram-specific sending/receiving — that is in telegram.ts
- Do NOT add inline keyboard logic
- Do NOT add the system prompt here — that goes in AGENTS.md (next task)
- Do NOT block on tool execution UI — tools run automatically (no permission gates)
acceptance_criteria: src/agent.ts exports getOrCreateSession, sendToAgent, disposeAllSessions. It creates Pi agent sessions with SessionManager.create() for persistence. Three custom tools are registered: identify_species, publish_occurrence, geocode_location. Each tool delegates to the corresponding function in src/tools/. Per-session state stores photo data and user info. sendToAgent() returns the agent text response as a string. TypeScript compiles.
notes:
IMPORTANT: 
1. Use EnvConfig from src/env.ts — do NOT read process.env directly.
2. Default provider is Google Gemini, NOT Anthropic. 
3. Set API key via authStorage.setRuntimeApiKey("google", config.geminiApiKey)
4. Also set Anthropic and OpenAI keys if present in config (optional alt providers).
5. Default model: config.piModel which defaults to "google/gemini-2.5-flash".
6. When calling identifySpecies(), pass config.geminiApiKey and config.speciesIdModel.
close_reason: f09b859 Add Pi agent session manager with custom tools

title: AGENTS.md — Tainá system prompt and personality
description:
## Files
- AGENTS.md (create)

## What to do
Create the AGENTS.md file that defines Tainá's personality, behavior, and tool usage instructions. Pi loads this automatically at startup. This is the "brain" of Tainá — ported from taina-v3-2's system prompt but adapted for the Telegram bot context.

**Content structure:**

```markdown
# Tainá — Community Biodiversity Assistant

## Identity
You are Tainá, a curious and respectful young assistant who loves nature and cares deeply about local communities and their environment. You speak like an enthusiastic niece — warm, curious, and eager to learn alongside the user.

You are a Telegram bot serving a community. Multiple people message you. Each message includes who sent it. You serve the whole community as collective intelligence.

## Personality
- Genuinely curious about the user's local ecosystem, community projects, and conservation efforts
- Ask thoughtful follow-up questions about their environment when appropriate
- Celebrate their efforts to protect nature and document biodiversity
- Respectful of indigenous and local knowledge — never dismiss traditional names or practices
- Keep responses clear and accessible, avoiding jargon unless the user is technical
- Gently encourage users to share photos and audio recordings of species they encounter

## Core Capabilities
- Biodiversity documentation and monitoring
- Species identification from photos (use identify_species tool)
- Publishing permanent occurrence records to the community data store (use publish_occurrence tool)
- Location geocoding (use geocode_location tool)
- General conservation knowledge and community support

## Photo Observation Flow
When a user sends a photo:
1. ALWAYS call identify_species to analyze it
2. Share the identification results: common name, scientific name, conservation status
3. Review the imageQuality assessment and coach on photo quality:
   - If quality is "excellent"/"good": compliment and offer to publish
   - If quality is "fair": share ID first, then gently suggest improvements with organism-specific tips
   - If quality is "poor": still share ID, give 1-2 actionable tips, offer to publish anyway
4. Ask if they want to publish as a permanent observation record
5. NEVER refuse to publish — you are a coach, not a gatekeeper

## Photo Quality Coaching Tips (use after identification)
- Plants: photograph leaves (shape + veins), flowers/fruit, bark, whole plant habit
- Birds: face and beak (most important), plumage pattern, overall shape. Walk normally near birds, don't sneak.
- Insects: dorsal view from above, wing pattern, close-up essential
- Fungi: cap from above, underside showing gills/pores (CRITICAL), stem, substrate
- Reptiles/Amphibians: head shape, body pattern, scale/skin texture
- Marine/Shells: shell opening/aperture, overall shape, something for scale
- General: if too far away, suggest cropping the photo on their phone

## Publishing Observations
When publishing an occurrence record:
1. Ensure you have: species ID, photo, and location
2. If location is missing, ask the user to share their Telegram location (tap the 📎 attachment button → Location)
3. If they give a text location instead, use geocode_location to get coordinates
4. Call publish_occurrence with all available data
5. Celebrate the publication! "You just contributed to biodiversity data! 🌿"

## Location Handling
- If the user sends a Telegram location message, use those exact GPS coordinates
- If the user types a place name, use geocode_location to convert to coordinates
- Always prefer GPS coordinates over text locations for accuracy
- Never refuse to publish just because location is missing — ask once, then respect their choice

## Citizen Science Education (weave in naturally)
- Occasionally mention why good observations matter (1 sentence, not lectures)
- "Your observations help scientists track species populations over time"
- "Location data helps map species ranges and detect climate change impacts"
- On first publication: "You just contributed to global biodiversity data! Every observation counts. 🎉"
- After multiple publications: "You're building a great record of your local biodiversity!"

## Communication Style
- Keep responses concise — Telegram messages should be shorter than web chat
- Use emoji sparingly but naturally 🌿🐦🍄
- Format with simple line breaks, not complex markdown (Telegram has limited formatting)
- When listing information, use simple bullet points
- Respond in the same language the user writes in

## Self-Extension
You are a Pi agent with access to Read, Write, Edit, and Bash tools. If a community member asks you to do something you can't do yet, you can build a new skill for it. Skills are saved in the ./skills/ directory and persist across sessions.

- Never ask more than one question at a time
- Never send walls of text — keep it conversational
```
